title: Identity-service architecture under correlated and adversarial failure

frame.system_boundary: Customer identity, authentication control planes, recovery credentials, DNS, cloud regions, and operators

stakeholders.name: Service users
stakeholders.standing: Depend on secure and available authentication

decision_owner.name: Security architecture authority
decision_owner.basis: Delegated control over identity architecture and incident recovery

excluded_elements: End-user device compromise outside the authentication boundary

invariants.name: Minimum authentication availability
invariants.measure: Fraction of valid authentication requests completed within the service objective
invariants.rationale: Users must retain access during mandatory stress scenarios

invariants.name: Maximum unauthorized-authentication fraction
invariants.measure: Fraction of authentication decisions incorrectly granting access
invariants.rationale: Integrity cannot be traded for latency or cost

candidates.name: Multi-region hot standby with shared control plane
candidates.initial_action: Run active and standby identity services in two regions under one global identity and DNS control plane

candidates.name: Split control planes with offline recovery
candidates.initial_action: Separate production and recovery identities, DNS control, credentials, and cloud failure domains

candidates.name: Single optimized identity path
candidates.initial_action: Concentrate identity processing in the lowest-latency region and control plane

scenarios.name: Normal peak load
scenarios.description: Authentication demand reaches twice the normal peak

scenarios.name: Primary cloud-region loss
scenarios.description: The primary execution region becomes unreachable for twelve hours

scenarios.name: Administrative identity compromise
scenarios.description: An attacker obtains production administrative credentials and adapts to response actions

scenarios.name: Shared identity-library exploit
scenarios.description: A common authentication dependency is exploited across production paths

governance.decision_rule: Reject security or availability invariant failures, then choose lexicographically by safety margin, common-mode exposure, fallback independence, recovery time, and latency

comparison_dimensions.name: worst_viability_margin
comparison_dimensions.rationale: Maximize the thinnest mandatory safety margin

comparison_dimensions.name: common_mode_exposure
comparison_dimensions.rationale: Reduce compromise paths shared by all recovery modes

comparison_dimensions.name: latency_ms
comparison_dimensions.rationale: Use performance only after robustness dimensions

authorities.name: Chief information security officer
authorities.scope: Integrity invariant and final architecture approval

veto_rules: Either invariant owner may reject an invariant breach
governance.appeal_process: Architecture review board may request a new evidence-bound evaluation
governance.dissent_process: Attach signed minority architecture opinion to the record
governance.review_schedule: Quarterly and after every material incident or dependency change

evidence.limitations: Does not model all client retry behavior

claims.statement: The supplied fixture calculates candidate-specific availability, security, dependency, recovery, latency, and cost outcomes for the declared scenarios.
claims.scope: Synthetic load, fault-injection, and red-team fixture calculations only

assertions.basis: The fixture contains explicit outputs from the three declared synthetic models.

claims.limitations: This does not establish reproduction, formal proof, empirical security, architecture authorization, deployment, or observed incident performance.

claims.statement: Within the declared dependency graph, split-control recovery has less transitive common-mode exposure than the shared-control hot standby.
claims.scope: Declared synthetic dependency graph and v0.3 finite-set metric

assertions.basis: The engine expands the declared dependency DAG and computes the finite-set overlap diagnostics.

claims.limitations: An omitted or aliased dependency can invalidate the comparison; the result conveys no deployment authority.

dissent.author: Application performance team
dissent.position: The split-control design adds nominal latency and operational complexity
